'''Enrique Jose Galvez''' is a Charles A. Dana professor of physics and astronomy at [[Colgate University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Enrique (Kiko) Galvez |url=https://www.colgate.edu/about/directory/egalvez |access-date=2026-04-04 |website=Colgate University |language=en}}</ref> His work focuses on [[Atomic, molecular, and optical physics|optical physics]] as well as improving undergraduate laboratories.<ref name=":2" />

== Education and career ==
Galvez pursued his undergraduate degree at [[Pontifical Catholic University of Peru]], graduating with a Bachelor's of Science in 1980.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Stowe |first=Gene |title=APS Honors Physics Alumnus Enrique Galvez |url=https://science.nd.edu/news-and-media/news/aps-honors-physics-alumnus-enrique-galvez/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240604152812/https://science.nd.edu/news-and-media/news/aps-honors-physics-alumnus-enrique-galvez/ |archive-date=2024-06-04 |access-date=2026-04-30 |website=College of Science |language=en-US}}</ref> He then obtained his PhD from the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 1986. He did his post-doc at [[Stony Brook University]] before joining Colgate University in 1988 as faculty, where he currently works.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Experiments on Photon Quantum Mechanics |url=https://advlab.org/Imm2021Colgate_PQM |access-date=2026-04-04 |website=ALPhA Advanced Laboraties}}</ref><ref name=":4" />

== Research and publications ==
Galvez focuses on working with shaped [[Light beam|optical beams]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Enrique Galvez |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/fellow_profiles/enrique_galvez/ |access-date=2026-04-04 |website=Optica|last=Gass|first=Jeanette}}</ref> He has worked in areas of [[quantum optics]], classical optics, and [[atomic physics]].<ref name=":1" /> He is also the coauthor of three physics textbooks.<ref name=":1" /> He is currently working on [[Quantum entanglement|photon entanglement]] and light in vector and scalar modes.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Enrique Galvez |url=https://spie.org/profile/Enrique.Galvez-54079 |access-date=2026-04-04 |website=SPIE}}</ref>
== Recognition ==
In 2024, he was named an [[American Physical Society]] fellow for mentoring undergraduate students in research and coursework as well as contributing to the design of approaches that help undergraduates learn quantum sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forum on Education Fellowship |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship/fed-fellowship |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=American Physical Society |language=en}}</ref> In 2020, he was the recipient of the Jonathan F. Reichert & Barbara Wolff-Reichert Award for Excellence in Advanced Laboratory Instruction for developing advanced labs that give students direct exposure to quantum mechanics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jonathan F. Reichert & Barbara Wolff-Reichert Award for Excellence in Advanced Laboratory Instruction |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/award/excellence-advanced-laboratory-instruction |access-date=2026-04-04 |website=American Physical Society}}</ref> In 2019 and 2020 he was named the Community Champion by the [[SPIE|International Society for Optics and Photonics]] (SPIE).<ref name=":3" /> In 2019, he was selected as a fellow of the [[Optica (society)|Optical Society of America]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 Fellows |url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/elected_fellows/2019_fellows/ |access-date=2026-04-04 |website=Optica}}</ref>
